title: Things to Do in Rishikesh: Rafting, Yoga, Ganga Aarti & Himalayan Treks

description: The best things to do in Rishikesh: white-water rafting on the Ganga, bungee and ziplines, yoga and ashrams, the Parmarth Niketan aarti, the Beatles Ashram, Kunjapuri sunrise, waterfalls and riverside cafés.

hero.alt: Rafters on white water on the Ganga near Rishikesh
hero.caption: Rafting on the Ganga

intro: Rishikesh sits where the Ganga emerges from the Garhwal Himalaya into the plains, about 25 km upstream from Haridwar in Uttarakhand. It has long been a place of pilgrimage and study, with ashrams lining both banks, and it calls itself the Yoga Capital of the World. Since the 1990s it has also become India's best-known base for white-water rafting.

That combination is what makes Rishikesh unusual. On the same day you can run rapids, jump from India's highest fixed bungee platform, attend a yoga class and watch the evening aarti by the river. The town is vegetarian and alcohol is not served in the main areas.
Five days lets you do all of this without rushing. October to November and March to April are the best months; rafting stops during the monsoon, roughly June to September.

sections.heading: Adventure activities in Rishikesh
sections.intro: All adventure operators in Rishikesh should be licensed by the state; ask to see the licence and check the safety equipment before booking.

items.name: Go white-water rafting
body: Rafting trips run on stretches of the Ganga upstream of town and end near Rishikesh. The most popular are the 16 km run from Shivpuri, with rapids graded around II to III+ such as Roller Coaster and Golf Course, and the longer 26 km run from Marine Drive. Beginners can start with the short Brahmpuri stretch.
No experience is needed, as each raft has a trained guide. Trips include a safety briefing, and many stop at a beach for cliff jumping or body surfing in calm water.

facts.Where: Shivpuri, Marine Drive and Brahmpuri put-in points
facts.Best time: October to November, March to May
facts.Good for: Teens and adults; age limits apply

items.name: Bungee jump, zipline or swing
body: At Mohan Chatti, about 20 km from Rishikesh, a cantilever platform over a gorge is home to one of India's highest fixed bungee jumps, run by an operator with international safety standards. The same site has a flying fox zipline and a giant swing. Book ahead in peak season and check weight and age limits.

items.name: Camp by the river
body: Beach and forest camps along the Ganga upstream of Rishikesh, especially around Shivpuri, combine rafting with a night in tents, bonfires and volleyball on the sand. Standards vary; choose camps with proper toilets and good reviews.

items.name: Hike to Kunjapuri for sunrise
body: Kunjapuri Devi Temple, on a hilltop above Narendra Nagar, is reached by road and a flight of steps. On a clear morning you see the Garhwal Himalaya, including peaks such as Bandarpunch and Chaukhamba, turning pink at sunrise. Many visitors drive up in the dark and walk the final steps; some walk down the forest trail afterwards.

items.name: Try kayaking, mountain biking or trekking
body: Kayaking courses, mountain biking along forest roads and short treks to waterfalls such as Patna Falls are all available. Rishikesh is also the starting point for longer Himalayan treks and the Char Dham pilgrimage.

items.name: Take a yoga or meditation class
body: Dozens of ashrams and schools offer drop-in classes, week-long retreats and 200-hour teacher training courses. Parmarth Niketan, Sivananda Ashram and many smaller schools around Tapovan and Laxman Jhula welcome beginners. The International Yoga Festival is held every March.

facts.Time needed: From a single class to a month-long course

items.name: Watch the Ganga Aarti

image.alt: Evening Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan, Rishikesh
image.caption: Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan

body: The evening aarti at Parmarth Niketan's ghat is calmer and more musical than Haridwar's, with devotional singing, lamps and a large Shiva statue by the river. Triveni Ghat, in the older part of town, has a more traditional aarti. Arrive before sunset to find a place on the steps.

items.name: Explore the Beatles Ashram

image.alt: Painted meditation domes at the Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia), Rishikesh
image.caption: Beatles Ashram

body: The former ashram of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi, where the Beatles stayed in 1968 and wrote many songs, was abandoned for decades and is now managed by the forest department. Its meditation domes and buildings are covered in murals, making it one of the most photogenic places in Rishikesh.

facts.Where: Near Swarg Ashram, inside Rajaji Tiger Reserve

items.name: Visit Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
body: Neelkanth Mahadev, about 30 km from Rishikesh in the forested hills, marks the place where Shiva is said to have drunk the poison from the churning of the ocean. The drive is scenic; some pilgrims trek the older route through the forest. It is extremely busy during the Kanwar Yatra in the monsoon.

items.name: Cross Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula

image.alt: Ram Jhula suspension bridge over the Ganga, Rishikesh
image.caption: Ram Jhula

body: The iron suspension bridges of Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula are Rishikesh's landmarks, linking temples and ashrams on either bank. Laxman Jhula was closed for safety reasons in recent years, and a replacement bridge with glass walkway sections has been under construction beside it; check which crossings are open when you visit. Walking across, with the river below and temples on both banks, is part of every visit.

items.name: Visit Neer Garh Waterfall

image.alt: Neer Garh Waterfall in the forest near Rishikesh
image.caption: Neer Garh Waterfall

body: A short walk from the road beyond Laxman Jhula leads through forest to Neer Garh's series of cascades and pools. It is best after the monsoon, from September to November.

items.name: Spend an afternoon in Tapovan's cafés
body: The Tapovan and Laxman Jhula area is full of relaxed cafés with river views, serving everything from Israeli and Italian food to thalis and fresh juices, alongside bookshops and yoga-wear stores. It is where many visitors spend their downtime.

items.name: Take a day trip to Haridwar
body: Haridwar, 25 km downstream, has the grand evening aarti at Har ki Pauri, hilltop temples reached by ropeway and busy bazaars.

byTraveller.text: Riverside camping, sunrise at Kunjapuri, rafting together, sunset at the Parmarth aarti and café evenings in Tapovan.
The Brahmpuri rafting stretch for older children, the aarti, bridges, Neer Garh Waterfall and the Beatles Ashram. Choose camps with proper facilities.
Rishikesh is one of India's easiest places to travel alone, with yoga courses, group rafting trips and a sociable café scene.
The 16 km rafting run, a camp night with bonfire, and bungee at Mohan Chatti.

oneDay: Raft the Shivpuri stretch in the morning. After lunch in Tapovan, walk across Laxman Jhula and Ram Jhula, then explore the Beatles Ashram. Finish at Parmarth Niketan for the evening Ganga Aarti.
tips: Rishikesh is a vegetarian town and alcohol is not served in the main areas.
Book rafting only with licensed operators, and check life jackets and helmets before setting off.
Rafting is closed during the monsoon, roughly June to September, when the river is too high.
Dehradun's Jolly Grant Airport is about 35 km away; Haridwar and Rishikesh have railway stations.
Weekends see large crowds from Delhi; weekdays are much calmer.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Rishikesh?
faqs.a: White-water rafting, bungee jumping at Mohan Chatti, yoga classes, the Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan, the Beatles Ashram, a sunrise at Kunjapuri, riverside camping and the cafés of Tapovan.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Rishikesh?
faqs.a: Five days lets you combine rafting, bungee, yoga, the Beatles Ashram, a Kunjapuri sunrise and a day trip to Haridwar without rushing. Two to three days covers the highlights.

faqs.q: When is rafting open in Rishikesh?
faqs.a: Rafting generally runs from September or October to June and closes during the monsoon. October and November, and March to May, are the best months.
Yes. Riverside camps, rafting, sunrise hikes, the evening aarti and quiet cafés make it a popular short break for couples.
Yes, with the shorter Brahmpuri rafting stretch for older children, the aarti, waterfalls and bridges. Most adventure activities have minimum age limits.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Rishikesh?
faqs.a: October to November and March to April for good weather and rafting. The monsoon brings heavy rain and closes rafting.
